[2026-11-25T08:13:09.773Z] [INFO]         "content": "# @link-foundation/universal-translator\n\nTranslate programs between languages through a typed meta language, with\nmatching JavaScript and Rust implementations. The translator is built from\ngrammar and rule tables, not from per-program templates. It reads JavaScript,\nTypeScript, Python, Ruby, Lua, PHP, C, C++, C#, Java, Go, Rust, Kotlin,\nSwift, Perl, Dart, Scala, Julia, R, Groovy, Objective-C, Nim, D, Pascal,\nFortran, Ada, Visual Basic .NET, Bash, MATLAB/Octave, Zig, Lean 4 and Rocq\n(32 languages), and writes any of them. It can also lower a program to x86-64\nassembly (NASM), CIL (ILAsm) or JVM bytecode (Jasmin).\n\n## Translate a program\n\n```sh\nnpm ci\nnode bin/universal-translator.js translate javascript python examples/programs/factorial.js\nnode bin/universal-translator.js translate python rust - < program.py\nnode bin/universal-translator.js translate javascript nasm examples/programs/fizz-buzz.js\nnode bin/universal-translator.js meta go examples/programs/hand-written/sum-of-squares.go\nnode bin/universal-translator.js languages\ncargo run --locked -- translate-grammar javascript kotlin examples/programs/factorial.js\n```\n\nBoth CLIs read a file, or standard input when you omit the file or pass `-`.\nThe JavaScript package supports Node.js 20 and later, Bun and Deno.\n\nEach translation runs these stages:\n\n1. A lexer and a table-driven parser read the source language.\n2. Understanding rules turn the syntax tree into a meta program.\n3. Type inference gives every value a type.\n4. Meaning rules and any configured meta→meta layers rewrite the program.\n5. Context rules adapt it to the target language.\n6. An emitter writes the target syntax. For the machine targets, the program\n   is first lowered to a stack machine.\n\nPick a mode with `--mode`:\n\n- `context-dependent` (the default) adapts names, comments and terms such as\n  \"function\" or \"method\" to the target language.\n- `literal` keeps names and comment text as written.\n- `same-effect` keeps only what the program does and may restructure it.\n\nThe meta language has integers, text, booleans and integer arrays. Arrays\nare indexed from 0 in the meta language, and languages that count from 1\nshift every index. In C an array is a local variable-length array, so its\nlength is `sizeof a / sizeof a[0]`. The sieve, bubble sort and sum and\nproduct examples use arrays. The case study lists the other compromises.\n\n`createTranslator({ layers })` takes rule layers that can be replaced or\ndecorated. The common library in `common-library/` only hides differences\nbetween standard libraries, such as printing. `--common-library` translates\nevery print into a call to it.\n\nEvery program in `examples/programs` has been translated into every target\nin `examples/programs/translated`. These shared files are what the JavaScript\nand Rust tests check against. `node examples/programs/verify-native.mjs`\ncompiles and runs each translation with its native toolchain, and CI runs it\nwith `--require-all`.\n\n## Translate a statement or a function on its own\n\nA fragment is a whole program, one or more function definitions, or one or\nmore statements. `parseFragment` tries the source in that order and\nreturns its kind. `translateFragment` writes the same kind of fragment\nin the target, without a main function, a class or imports.\n\n```js\nimport {\n  parseFragment,\n  translateFragment,\n} from '@link-foundation/universal-translator';\n\nparseFragment('x = x + 1;', 'javascript').kind; // 'statements'\ntranslateFragment('x = x + 1;', 'javascript', 'pascal'); // 'x := x + 1;\\n'\ntranslateFragment('def square(n):\\n    return n * n\\n', 'python', 'rust');\n// 'fn square(n: i64) -> i64 {\\n    return n * n;\\n}\\n'\n```\n\n```sh\necho 'x = x + 1;' | node bin/universal-translator.js translate javascript pascal --fragment\n```\n\nThe Rust crate has `parse_fragment` and `translate_fragment`, as free\nfunctions and as methods of `Translator`, and its command line has the same\n`--fragment` flag. A fragment must be complete. A function ends with its\nclosing, a block statement with its end, and a single line statement is a\nwhole statement. Otherwise the error says what is missing and where, for\nexample `The fragment is not complete: it ends before its closing (line 2)`.\n\nEvery fragment in `examples/programs/fragments` is translated into every\nlanguage under `examples/programs/fragments/translated`. Both test suites\ncheck these files and read each of them back into the same JavaScript.\n\nLimits:\n\n- Variables that the fragment uses but does not declare stay undeclared.\n  Pascal, Fortran and Ada only declare the variables that the fragment\n  declares itself, and keep the spelling of the others as written. In Zig\n  such a variable is printed with `{any}`.\n- In Python, Ruby and other languages without declarations, `x = 5` is read\n  as a declaration.\n- In a natural language, a fragment is one or more sentences that match a\n  template of the language.\n- Machine targets (NASM, CIL, JVM) hold whole programs only. A statement or\n  function on its own is rejected.\n- Perl and Bash have no booleans, so `true` and `false` come back as 1 and 0.\n- Classes are not part of the meta language yet.\n\n## Translate to and from controlled natural languages\n\nControlled versions of 30 natural languages are languages like any other.\nThey are English, Chinese, Hindi, Spanish, French, Arabic, Bengali,\nPortuguese, Russian, Urdu, Indonesian, German, Japanese, Marathi, Telugu,\nTurkish, Tamil, Vietnamese, Korean, Italian, Persian, Swahili, Tagalog,\nThai, Polish, Ukrainian, Hausa, Gujarati, Punjabi and Dutch. Each one is\ndescribed as data in `data/natural/<id>.lino`: one sentence template for\nevery meta statement, one phrase for every operator, and a small lexicon\nfor program names. The writer and the reader use the same tables, so every\nsentence the writer produces is one the reader accepts.\n\n```sh\nnode bin/universal-translator.js translate javascript russian examples/programs/fizz-buzz.js\nnode bin/universal-translator.js translate english rust examples/programs/natural/factorial/factorial.english.txt\nnode bin/universal-translator.js translate nasm minimal-english examples/programs/translated/factorial/factorial.asm\nnode bin/universal-translator.js check-words english-e-prime examples/programs/natural/leap-year/leap-year.english-e-prime.txt\n```\n\n```text\nДля каждого число от 1 до 100 повторять это:\n  Если число по модулю 15 равно 0, сделать это:\n    Написать «FizzBuzz» и закончить строку.\n```\n\nProfiles extend a language and add the rules of a controlled language\nstandard. `checkText` and `check-words` enforce those rules:\n\n| Profile                   | Standard                                     | Rules that are checked                                |\n| ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | [2026-11-25T08:13:09.773Z] [INFO]     "stdout": "# @link-foundation/universal-translator\n\nTranslate programs between languages through a typed meta language, with\nmatching JavaScript and Rust implementations. The translator is built from\ngrammar and rule tables, not from per-program templates. It reads JavaScript,\nTypeScript, Python, Ruby, Lua, PHP, C, C++, C#, Java, Go, Rust, Kotlin,\nSwift, Perl, Dart, Scala, Julia, R, Groovy, Objective-C, Nim, D, Pascal,\nFortran, Ada, Visual Basic .NET, Bash, MATLAB/Octave, Zig, Lean 4 and Rocq\n(32 languages), and writes any of them. It can also lower a program to x86-64\nassembly (NASM), CIL (ILAsm) or JVM bytecode (Jasmin).\n\n## Translate a program\n\n```sh\nnpm ci\nnode bin/universal-translator.js translate javascript python examples/programs/factorial.js\nnode bin/universal-translator.js translate python rust - < program.py\nnode bin/universal-translator.js translate javascript nasm examples/programs/fizz-buzz.js\nnode bin/universal-translator.js meta go examples/programs/hand-written/sum-of-squares.go\nnode bin/universal-translator.js languages\ncargo run --locked -- translate-grammar javascript kotlin examples/programs/factorial.js\n```\n\nBoth CLIs read a file, or standard input when you omit the file or pass `-`.\nThe JavaScript package supports Node.js 20 and later, Bun and Deno.\n\nEach translation runs these stages:\n\n1. A lexer and a table-driven parser read the source language.\n2. Understanding rules turn the syntax tree into a meta program.\n3. Type inference gives every value a type.\n4. Meaning rules and any configured meta→meta layers rewrite the program.\n5. Context rules adapt it to the target language.\n6. An emitter writes the target syntax. For the machine targets, the program\n   is first lowered to a stack machine.\n\nPick a mode with `--mode`:\n\n- `context-dependent` (the default) adapts names, comments and terms such as\n  \"function\" or \"method\" to the target language.\n- `literal` keeps names and comment text as written.\n- `same-effect` keeps only what the program does and may restructure it.\n\nThe meta language has integers, text, booleans and integer arrays. Arrays\nare indexed from 0 in the meta language, and languages that count from 1\nshift every index. In C an array is a local variable-length array, so its\nlength is `sizeof a / sizeof a[0]`. The sieve, bubble sort and sum and\nproduct examples use arrays. The case study lists the other compromises.\n\n`createTranslator({ layers })` takes rule layers that can be replaced or\ndecorated. The common library in `common-library/` only hides differences\nbetween standard libraries, such as printing. `--common-library` translates\nevery print into a call to it.\n\nEvery program in `examples/programs` has been translated into every target\nin `examples/programs/translated`. These shared files are what the JavaScript\nand Rust tests check against. `node examples/programs/verify-native.mjs`\ncompiles and runs each translation with its native toolchain, and CI runs it\nwith `--require-all`.\n\n## Translate a statement or a function on its own\n\nA fragment is a whole program, one or more function definitions, or one or\nmore statements. `parseFragment` tries the source in that order and\nreturns its kind. `translateFragment` writes the same kind of fragment\nin the target, without a main function, a class or imports.\n\n```js\nimport {\n  parseFragment,\n  translateFragment,\n} from '@link-foundation/universal-translator';\n\nparseFragment('x = x + 1;', 'javascript').kind; // 'statements'\ntranslateFragment('x = x + 1;', 'javascript', 'pascal'); // 'x := x + 1;\\n'\ntranslateFragment('def square(n):\\n    return n * n\\n', 'python', 'rust');\n// 'fn square(n: i64) -> i64 {\\n    return n * n;\\n}\\n'\n```\n\n```sh\necho 'x = x + 1;' | node bin/universal-translator.js translate javascript pascal --fragment\n```\n\nThe Rust crate has `parse_fragment` and `translate_fragment`, as free\nfunctions and as methods of `Translator`, and its command line has the same\n`--fragment` flag. A fragment must be complete. A function ends with its\nclosing, a block statement with its end, and a single line statement is a\nwhole statement. Otherwise the error says what is missing and where, for\nexample `The fragment is not complete: it ends before its closing (line 2)`.\n\nEvery fragment in `examples/programs/fragments` is translated into every\nlanguage under `examples/programs/fragments/translated`. Both test suites\ncheck these files and read each of them back into the same JavaScript.\n\nLimits:\n\n- Variables that the fragment uses but does not declare stay undeclared.\n  Pascal, Fortran and Ada only declare the variables that the fragment\n  declares itself, and keep the spelling of the others as written. In Zig\n  such a variable is printed with `{any}`.\n- In Python, Ruby and other languages without declarations, `x = 5` is read\n  as a declaration.\n- In a natural language, a fragment is one or more sentences that match a\n  template of the language.\n- Machine targets (NASM, CIL, JVM) hold whole programs only. A statement or\n  function on its own is rejected.\n- Perl and Bash have no booleans, so `true` and `false` come back as 1 and 0.\n- Classes are not part of the meta language yet.\n\n## Translate to and from controlled natural languages\n\nControlled versions of 30 natural languages are languages like any other.\nThey are English, Chinese, Hindi, Spanish, French, Arabic, Bengali,\nPortuguese, Russian, Urdu, Indonesian, German, Japanese, Marathi, Telugu,\nTurkish, Tamil, Vietnamese, Korean, Italian, Persian, Swahili, Tagalog,\nThai, Polish, Ukrainian, Hausa, Gujarati, Punjabi and Dutch. Each one is\ndescribed as data in `data/natural/<id>.lino`: one sentence template for\nevery meta statement, one phrase for every operator, and a small lexicon\nfor program names. The writer and the reader use the same tables, so every\nsentence the writer produces is one the reader accepts.\n\n```sh\nnode bin/universal-translator.js translate javascript russian examples/programs/fizz-buzz.js\nnode bin/universal-translator.js translate english rust examples/programs/natural/factorial/factorial.english.txt\nnode bin/universal-translator.js translate nasm minimal-english examples/programs/translated/factorial/factorial.asm\nnode bin/universal-translator.js check-words english-e-prime examples/programs/natural/leap-year/leap-year.english-e-prime.txt\n```\n\n```text\nДля каждого число от 1 до 100 повторять это:\n  Если число по модулю 15 равно 0, сделать это:\n    Написать «FizzBuzz» и закончить строку.\n```\n\nProfiles extend a language and add the rules of a controlled language\nstandard. `checkText` and `check-words` enforce those rules:\n\n| Profile                   | Standard                                     | Rules that are checked                                |\n| ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |\n| `english` (`cnl-default`) | Balanced intersection of the standards below | One-to-one single-word lexicon; every text reads back |\n| `english-asd-ste100`      | ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English      | At most 20 words, imperative starts, word list        |\n| `english-ace`             | Attempto Controlled English                  | Sentences start with ACE's determiners and keywords   |\n| `english-gellish`         | Gellish Formal English                       | Templates use each listed Gellish relation phrase     |\n| `dutch-gellish`           | Gellish Formeel Nederlands                   | Templates use each listed Gellish relation phrase     |\n| `english-sbvr`            | SBVR Structured English                      | Sentences start with SBVR keywords                    |\n| `english-plain-language`  | Plain language (ISO 24495-1)                 | At most 25 words, 20 on average; no \"shall\"           |\n| `english-e-prime`         | E-Prime                                      | No form of \"to be\"                                    |\n| `english-basic-english`   | Basic English (Ogden's 850 words)            | At most 25 words; template words from Ogden's list    |\n| `english-special-english` | VOA Special English / Learning English       | Template words from its word list, short sentences    |\n| `english-globish`         | Globish                                      | At most 20 words; template words from Globish list The template's release\nhistory is kept in\n[docs/template-history/CHANGELOG.md](docs/template-history/CHANGELOG.md).\n\n## Features\n\n- **Multi-runtime support**: Works with Bun, Node.js, and Deno\n- **Universal testing**: Uses [test-anywhere](https://github.com/link-foundation/test-anywhere) for cross-runtime tests\n- **Automated releases**: Changesets-based versioning with GitHub Actions\n- **Optional Docker Hub publishing**: Docker images can be published after the matching npm version is visible\n- **Universal app example**: React UI for the package API with GitHub Pages, Electron, and Capacitor build paths\n- **Code quality**: ESLint + Prettier with pre-commit hooks via Husky\n- **Package manager agnostic**: Works with bun, npm, yarn, pnpm, and deno\n- **Broken link checks**: Automated link validation with [lychee](https://github.com/lycheeverse/lychee-action) and Web Archive fallback suggestions\n\n## Quick Start\n\nThe documentation and demo site is built from LiNo with our own framework and\npublished at <https://link-foundation.github.io/ui/>. It includes English and\nRussian pages, theme preferences and development mode. See\n[the site workspace](packages/site/README.md) for local development.\n\n### Using the Package\n\n```bash\nnpm install @link-foundation/ui\n```\n\n```js\nimport { version } from '@link-foundation/ui';\n\nconsole.log(version);\n```\n\n### Importing HTML\n\n[`@link-foundation/ui-convert`](packages/ui-convert/README.md) turns an HTML\nstring or a live DOM subtree into a UI dialect document:\n\n```js\nimport { importHtml } from '@link-foundation/ui-convert';\n\nconsole.log(importHtml('<button id=\"ok\" class=\"primary\">OK</button>').text);\n// (ok: button\n//   (label OK)\n//   (attr class primary))\n```\n\nScripts, `on*` attributes and `javascript:` URLs are dropped with a\n`dropped-script` diagnostic; see the package README for the mapping table,\nids, spans and `importDom`.\n\n### Interop with A2UI, Adaptive Cards, JSON Forms and Lottie\n\nThe same package converts both ways between the UI dialect and\n[A2UI](https://a2ui.org), [Adaptive Cards](https://adaptivecards.io),\n[JSON Forms](https://jsonforms.io) and [Lottie](https://lottie.github.io):\n\n```bash\nnpx ui-convert import card.json > card.lino\nnpx ui-convert export card.lino --format adaptive-cards > card.json\n```\n\nSee the\n[capability matrix](packages/ui-convert/README.md#capability-matrix) for\nwhat each format supports.\n\n### Design tokens\n\n[`@link-foundation/ui-themes`](packages/ui-themes/README.md) ships the base\nLiNo theme. The [theme engine](docs/spec/themes.md) resolves inheritance,\ncontrast-safe colors and system preferences, and applies nested boundaries\nwithout replacing controls. Try the [four-panel example](examples/themes/README.md).\n\n[`@link-foundation/ui-tokens`](packages/ui-tokens/README.md) reads design\ntokens written in Links Notation, with inheritance, aliases and modes, and\nwrites them as CSS custom properties, DTCG 2025.10 JSON, Swift and Kotlin:\n\n```sh\nnpx link-ui-tokens build tokens.lino --set material3 \\\n  --css tokens.css --dtcg tokens.json --swift Tokens.swift --kotlin Tokens.kt\n```\n\n### Charts\n\n[`@link-foundation/ui-components`](packages/ui-components/README.md)\nrenders charts written in Links Notation with `data`, `mark` and\n`encoding` as deterministic, accessible SVG: `<ui-chart>` has a data table\ntwin and arrow-key navigation between points. ECharts is loaded only for\n`(renderer echarts)`:\n\n```html\n<ui-chart>\n  <script type=\"text/lino\">\n    (sales: chart\n      (description 'Sales grew from 12 to 30 thousand')\n      (data (row (month 2026-01) (value 12)) (row (month 2026-02) (value 30)))\n      (mark bar)\n      (encoding (x (field month) (type ordinal)) (y (field value) (type quantitative))))\n  </script>\n</ui-chart>\n```\n\n### DOM renderer\n\n[`@link-foundation/ui-dom`](packages/ui-dom/README.md) renders a document as\nplain custom elements in the light DOM (`ui-stack`, `ui-button`, …) with\nstable `data-link-id` attributes, patches only what each store transaction\nchanged, and dispatches `(on press ...)` handlers as `ui-action` events\nwithout running code:\n\n```js\nimport { mountDocument } from '@link-foundation/ui-dom';\n\nconst { store } = mountDocument(app, text, { tokens, styles, onAction });\nstore.setProp('greeting', 'value', ['Hello again']); // one patch\n```\n\n### React\n\n[`@link-foundation/ui-react`](packages/ui-react/README.md) mounts the ui-dom\nrenderer in a React tree. Store changes patch the DOM without re-rendering\n`<UiView>`; hooks such as `useUiProp` read the store, actions call host\nfunctions, and custom kinds can be React components:\n\n```jsx\nimport { UiView } from '@link-foundation/ui-react';\n\n<UiView\n  source=\"(ok: button (label 'OK') (on press (emit save)))\"\n  actions={{ save: () => console.log('saved') }}\n  components={{ chart: Chart }}\n/>;\n```\n\n### Vue\n\n[`@link-foundation/ui-vue`](packages/ui-vue/README.md) mounts ui-dom in a Vue 3\n`UiView` component, gives the store to Vue through composables\n(`useUiProp`, `useUiElement`, `useUiStore`, `useUiAction`) and draws custom\nkinds with Vue components ([example app](examples/vue/)):\n\n```js\nimport { UiView, createUiPlugin } from '@link-foundation/ui-vue';\n\napp.use(createUiPlugin({ store, actions: { save } })); // (on press (emit save))\n// <UiView :components=\"{ chart: SalesChart }\" @action=\"log\" />\n```\n\n### Animations\n\n[`@link-foundation/ui-animation`](packages/ui-animation/README.md) reads\nanimations written in Links Notation (keyframe tracks, easings, springs,\ntimelines with stagger, `(on pressed ...)` triggers and seeded procedural\neffects), samples them as pure functions of time, validates fills, WCAG\n2.3.1 flashes and reduced motion, and plays them on the Web Animations API.\nGSAP is never used:\n\n```js\nimport { createPlayer } from '@link-foundation/ui-animation';\n\nconst player = createPlayer(handle, { animations: text, resolveToken });\nplayer.bindTriggers(store); // (on pressed (play press-feedback))\nawait player.play('intro').finished;\n```\n\n### Behaviour and accessibility\n\n[`@link-foundation/ui-components`](packages/ui-components/README.md) adds\nbehaviour written as LiNo state machines (`toggle`, `disclosure`), an actions\nregistry that never evaluates code, and keyboard and focus helpers:\n\n```js\nimport { mountBehavior } from '@link-foundation/ui-components/behavior/dom';\n\nmountBehavior(\n  app,\n  `(page: document\n  (bold: button (label Bold) (machine toggle-machine)))`\n);\n// Enter, Space or a click switch Existing\n`draw(time, state)` callbacks remain supported; `time` is the animation-frame\nclock in milliseconds. The third argument is elapsed seconds since that effect's\nlast draw (initially zero, capped at 0.25); the fourth is `{scale, fps}`.\nReturn `true` to continue animating; any other return removes an animated effect.\n\n```js\nconst governor = createEffectGovernor({\n  watchVisibility: true,\n  watchReducedMotion: true,\n});\nconst remove = governor.add(\n  'background',\n  (time, state, elapsedSeconds, quality) => {\n    paintBackground(elapsedSeconds, quality.scale);\n    return true;\n  },\n  { fps: 30, onQualityChange: ({ scale }) => resizeBackingStore(scale) }\n);\ngovernor.set({ motion: 'auto' });\n// After a resize or option change, repaint once even if motion is off:\ngovernor.invalidate('background');\n// Read a detached snapshot at any time while the effect is registered:\nconsole.log(governor.getQuality('background'));\nremove();\ngovernor.dispose();\n```\n\nEach effect watches all animation frames, including frames skipped by its cap.\nGaps above 45 ms are slow; gaps at or below zero or above 1000 ms are ignored.\nWindows close after 30 valid gaps or 1000 accumulated milliseconds. The first\nwindow is warm-up. A strict slow majority lowers quality once per window:\nresolution multiplies by `scaleFactor` (default 0.7, rounded to three decimals)\nuntil `minScale` (0.4), then frame-rate share multiplies by `fpsFactor` (0.5)\nuntil `minFps` (0.25). Quality never increases. These four per-effect options\naccept positive numbers up to one; factors must be below one. `resolution: false`\nkeeps scale at one and lowers only frame rate.\n\nHosts with their own scheduler can import `createQualityWatcher` from the\nsame entry point. Call `feed(gapMs)` with raw display gaps, read the current\nshares with `snapshot()`, and call `reset()` after a suspension to warm up\nagain. The watcher creates no subscriptions or frame callbacks.\n\nAn optional `fps` target of 5..60 throttles draws to\n`1000 / (fps * quality.fps)` milliseconds; omitting it preserves drawing on every\nanimation frame at full quality, with a 60 fps base when quality lowers the\nframe-rate share. `onQualityChange` receives a detached snapshot once per step,\nbefore drawing, allowing a backing store to resize only when necessary.\n\n=== ui-react\n{\n  \"name\": \"@link-foundation/ui-react\",\n  \"version\": \"0.1.0\",\n  \"description\": \"React adapter of the associative UI framework written in Links Notation: a <UiView> that mounts the ui-dom renderer, a provider, DOM-free store hooks and React components for custom dialect kinds\",\n  \"type\": \"module\",\n  \"exports\": {\n    \".\": {\n      \"types\": \"./src/index.d.ts\",\n      \"default\": \"./src/index.js\"\n    },\n    \"./hooks\": {\n      \"types\": \"./src/hooks.d.ts\",\n      \"default\": \"./src/hooks.js\"\n    }\n  },\n  \"types\": \"./src/index.d.ts\",\n  \"files\": [\n    \"src/\",\n    \"README.md\",\n    \"LICENSE\"\n  ],\n  \"keywords\": [\n    \"ui\",\n    \"links-notation\",\n    \"react\",\n    \"adapter\",\n    \"hooks\",\n    \"custom-elements\"\n  ],\n  \"license\": \"Unlicense\",\n  \"repository\": {\n    \"type\": \"git\",\n    \"url\": \"git+https://github.com/link-foundation/ui.git\",\n    \"directory\": \"packages/ui-react\"\n  },\n  \"homepage\": \"https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/tree/main/packages/ui-react#readme\",\n  \"bugs\": {\n    \"url\": \"https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/issues\"\n  },\n  \"engines\": {\n# @link-foundation/ui-react\n\nThe React adapter of the associative UI framework. `<UiView>` mounts the\n[`@link-foundation/ui-dom`](../ui-dom/README.md) renderer into one\n`<div data-ui-root>` and leaves the document to it: a change in the\n[`ui-store`](../ui-store/README.md) store patches the DOM directly, and\n`<UiView>` itself does not re-render. React components can read the store\nthrough hooks built on `useSyncExternalStore`, handle the document's\n`(on press ...)` actions, and draw custom kinds through portals.\n\nRuntime dependencies: the workspace packages `ui-core`, `ui-store` and\n`ui-dom`. `react` and `react-dom` (18 or later) are peer dependencies.\n\n```jsx\nimport { UiView } from '@link-foundation/ui-react';\n\n<UiView\n  source={\n    \"(app: document (body: stack (ok: button (label 'OK') (on press (emit save)))))\"\n  }\n  actions={{ save: () => console.log('saved') }}\n/>;\n```\n\nrenders\n\n```html\n<div data-ui-root=\"\">\n  <ui-document data-link-id=\"app\">\n    <ui-stack data-link-id=\"body\">\n      <ui-button data-link-id=\"ok\"><button type=\"button\">OK</button></ui-button>\n    </ui-stack>\n  </ui-document>\n</div>\n```\n\nThe example app [`examples/react/`](../../examples/react/) (Vite + React)\nrenders the issue-1 sample document, a counter that changes `greeting`\nthrough the store, and a custom `chart` kind drawn by a React component:\n\n```bash\nnpm --prefix examples/react install\nnpm --prefix examples/react run dev    # or: run build\n```\n\n![The ui-react example in Chromium](../../docs/screenshots/ui-react-example.png)\n\n## `<UiView>`\n\n| Prop                                | Meaning                                                                            |\n| ----------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| `source`                            | Links Notation text; parsed once per distinct string.                              |\n| `store`                             | A ui-store store; wins over `source` and the provider's store.                     |\n| `parseOptions`                      | Options of ui-core `parse` for `source`.                                           |\n| `actions`                           | Host functions by action name, or a registry with `has(name)` and `dispatch(...)`. |\n| `onAction(detail, event)`           | Called for every action of this view, before its handler.                          |\n| `onDiagnostic`, `onPatch`           | Parse and render diagnostics; the store events of each applied patch.              |\n| `components`                        | React components of custom kinds: `{ chart: Chart }`.                              |\n| `kinds`                             | Extra ui-dom kind renderers of this view only.                                     |\n| `tokens`, `styles`, `theme`, `css`… | The ui-dom style options (ui-tokens and ui-style text).                            |\n| `ssr`                               | Inline the static HTML of the document; the client replaces it on mount.           |\n| `handleRef`                         | A ref that holds the ui-dom render handle (`nodeFor`, `flush`…) while mounted.     |\n| `className`, `style`, `id`          | Set on the `<div data-ui-root>` container.                                         |\n\nThe store is resolved once per render: `store` prop, then `source`, then\nthe store of the enclosing `<UiProvider>`. Without one, `<UiView>` throws.\nRender options are compared shallowly, so an inline `styles={text}` does\nnot remount the view; a new store, new options or new component kinds\ndestroy the old render and render again.\n\nKind renderers are passed to the ui-dom `render` of each view (the `kinds`\noption), not registered globally with `defineKind`, so two views never\nshare or leak kinds.\n\n## Actions\n\nAn action is data (docs/spec/behaviour.md): the document never runs code.\nA click on `ok` in the example above dispatches a `ui-action` event with\nthe detail `{ source: 'ok', event: 'press', action: ['emit', 'save'] }`.\n`<UiView>` calls `onAction(detail, event)`, then the first handler found by\nname:\n\n1. handlers registered with `useUiAction(name, handler)` inside the view or\n   provider (the last registration wins);\n2. the `actions` prop of the view;\n3. the enclosing `<UiProvider actions>`, outwards.\n\nFor `(emit NAME ...)` the name `NAME` is tried first, then `emit`; for any\nother action its head (`navigate`, `set`, `toggle`, `focus`). A plain\nhandler is called as `handler(detail, event)`; a registry gets\n`dispatch(name, args, { detail, event })`, where `args` are the values after\nthe name. When handlers are configured but none matches, a development\nwarning is logged (`[ui-react] no handler for the action ...`) and the\naction is ignored; production builds stay silent.\n\nThe vocabulary only knows the actions `navigate`, `emit`, `set`, `toggle`\nand `focus`, so `(on press (save))` gets an `unknown-action` diagnostic and\nis not bound. Write `(on press (emit save))` to call `actions.save`.\n\nEach view handles only the events of its own nodes, so nested views do not\nrun each other's handlers.\n\n## Hooks\n\n```jsx\nimport {\n  UiProvider,\n  useUiAction,\n  useUiProp,\n} from '@link-foundation/ui-react/hooks';\n\nfunction Greeting() {\n  // Re-renders only when this property of `greeting` changes.\n  const [text] = useUiProp('greeting', 'value') ?? Each link is written either\n`(id: kind clauses…)` or `(kind id clauses…)`; a link with an id and no kind\nis a setting.\n\n```\nschema    = (id: schema (version N))\nsection   = (id: section [(label 'Text')] [(description 'Text')])\nsetting   = (key: (type T) (default V…) clause…)\n          | (key: setting (type T) (default V…) clause…)\npreset    = (preset id [(label 'Text')] [(description 'Text')] (set key V…)…)\nmigration = (migration (from N) (to M) (rename old new)… (old-default key V…)…)\n```\n\nClauses of a setting:\n\n| Clause                                  | Meaning                                                                                                                                                |\n| --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |\n| `(type T)`                              | `range`, `number`, `toggle`, `choice`, `color`, `text` or a type added with `defineFieldType`.                                                         |\n| `(default V…)`                          | The default; it must coerce without change (`(default 99)` above `max` is an error).                                                                   |\n| `(min N)` `(max N)` `(step N)`          | Bounds and step of `range` (required: `min`, `max`) and `number`; values are clamped and rounded to the step grid that starts at `min`.                |\n| `(unit U)`                              | Appended to the CSS value (`24px`).                                                                                                                    |\n| `(options a b c)`                       | The options of `choice` (required).                                                                                                                    |\n| `(label 'Text')` `(description 'Text')` | For generated settings panels.                                                                                                                         |\n| `(section id)`                          | The section of the setting (an unknown section is a warning).                                                                                          |\n| `(comfort)`                             | A comfort setting: kept from the viewer when a shared look is opened, never randomised, ignored by `activePreset`. Presets that set one get a warning. |\n| `(apply (css-var --name))`              | Set as a CSS custom property on `<html>`.                                                                                                              |\n| `(apply (data-attr name))`              | Set as the attribute `data-name` on `<html>`.                                                                                                          |\n| anything else                           | Kept in `field.props` for custom types.                                                                                                                |\n\nKeys are names such as `liquid.blur` (letters, digits, `.`, `-`, `_`).\n`readSchema` never throws: problems are diagnostics (`missing-type`,\n`unknown-type`, `missing-default`, `bad-default`, `missing-range`,\n`missing-options`, `duplicate-key`, `bad-key`, `unknown-key`, `bad-value`,\n`bad-migration`, `bad-version`, `unknown-link`, `unknown-section`,\n`preset-sets-comfort`, `missing-schema-version`, syntax errors), and fields\nwith errors are left out of the schema.\n\n### Field types\n\n| Type     | Value                    | Raw values accepted                            | Random             |\n| -------- | ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------- | ------------------ |\n| `range`  | number in `[min, max]`   | numbers and decimal atoms (`'24'`, `'-0.5'`)   | on the step grid   |\n| `number` | number (bounds optional) | same                                           | when bounded       |\n| `toggle` | `true` / `false`         | booleans, `'true'`, `'false'`                  | yes                |\n| `choice` | one of `options`         | option strings (numbers are compared as text)  | one of the options |\n| `color`  | `#rrggbb`                | `#rrggbb` strings (`red`, `#fff` are rejected) | yes                |\n| `text`   | string                   | strings and numbers                            | never              |\n\n```js\nimport { defineFieldType } from '@link-foundation/ui-settings';\n\ndefineFieldType('vector3', {\n  coerce(field, raw) {\n    const parts = (Array.isArray(raw) ? raw : String(raw).split(' ')).map(\n      Number\n    );\n    return parts.length === 3 && parts.every(Number.isFinite)\n      ? { ok: true, value: parts }\n      : { ok: false };\n  },\n  equals: (a, b) => a.every((n, i) => n === b[i]),\n  random: (field, random) => [random(), random(), random()],\n  format: (field, value) => value.map(String), // (light.direction 0 0 1)\n});\n```\n\n`coerce` is required; `equals` defaults to structural equality, `random` to\n\"not randomised\", `format` to the value as atoms and `css` to the formatted\natoms joined with spaces. A `coerce` that throws counts as a rejected value.\n\n## Values\n\nValues are a plain object with a value for every field. Documents and share\nlinks hold only the values that differ from the defaults:\n\n```\n(settings (version 2) (liquid.blur 24))\n```\n\n| Function                                        | Result                                                                                                                       |\n| ----------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| `defaults(schema)`                              | Every default.                                                                                                               |\n| `merge(schema, base, untrusted)`                | `{ values, rejected }`: unknown keys, `__proto__` and values that do not coerce are rejected. Never throws.                  |\n| `diff(schema, values)`                          | Only the changed values, in schema order.                                                                                    |\n| `isDefault(schema, key, value)`                 | Whether the value is the default.                                                                                            |\n| `reset(schema, values, keys?)`                  | Some keys (default: all) back to the default.                                                                                |\n| `countCustomized(schema, values)`               | How many values differ from the defaults.                                                                                    |\n| `equalValues(schema, a, b, { skip })`           | Field-by-field equality; key order does not matter.                                                                          |\n| `applyPreset(schema, values, id)`               | The values with the preset applied (comfort settings keep their values).                                                     |\n| `activePreset(schema, values)`                  | The id of the preset the values match (ignoring comfort settings and key order), or `null`.                                  |\n| `randomize(schema, values, { random, locked })` | A random look; `random` is required, so a seeded generator gives the same look every time; comfort and locked keys are kept. |\n\n## Documents and share links\n\n| Function                                                | Result                                                                                                                |\n| ------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| `toLino(schema, values)`                                | `(settings (version N) (key value…)…)` of the changed values.                                                         |\n| `fromLino(schema, text, { base, look })`                | `{ ok, values, rejected, version, diagnostics }`, migrated to the schema version.                                     |\n| `fromLegacyJson(schema, json, { version, base, look })` | The JSON settings of the earlier sites.                                                                               |\n| `toShareHash(schema, values)`                           | `#settings=<encodeURIComponent(values document)>`.                                                                    |\n| `fromShareHash(schema, hash, viewerValues)`             | Reads `#settings=(settings …)`, `#settings={…}` (konard.github.io) and `#ui={…}` (immortality); `format` tells which. |\n\nShare links carry a shared _look_: when one is opened, every comfort setting\nkeeps the viewer's value. Hashes longer than `MAX_SHARE_HASH` (8 KiB) are\nrejected with the diagnostic `hash-too-large`, and nothing a link holds can\nthrow: bad encodings, bad JSON and unknown keys become diagnostics and\n`rejected` keys.\n\n## Migrations\n\n`(migration (from 1) (to 2) (rename blur liquid.blur) (old-default liquid.blur 12))`\nmoves version 1 values to version 2:\n\n1. keys are renamed (`blur` → `liquid.blur`);\n2. stored values equal to the old default are dropped, so the user gets the\n   new default (`(blur 12)` → `liquid.blur 18`, `(blur 30)` → `liquid.blur 30`);\n3. the result is merged onto the defaults (or `base`).\n\nMigrations chain (1 → 2 → 3). A shared look from an old version (`look: true`,\nused for share links) is different: the sender saw the old defaults, so\nmissing keys take the old defaults. A newer version than the schema is read\nas it is, with the warning `newer-version`.\n\n## Applying values before paint\n\n`applyToRoot(schema, values, root = document.documentElement)` sets the CSS\nvariables and data attributes of every applied setting (invalid values get the\ndefault).\n\nThe first paint must already use the stored values, so the page inlines a\nsmall script at the top of `<head>`:\n\n```js\nimport {\nShell cwd was reset to /tmp/gh-issue-solver-1795594347603",

[2026-11-25T08:13:52.982Z] [INFO]         "content": "# @link-foundation/ui-i18n\n\nLocalisation of [`@link-foundation/ui-core`](../ui-core/README.md) documents\nwith [lino-i18n](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-i18n) (pinned to\n0.5.0). Documents refer to catalog messages with `(t KEY)`; the locale is the\nroot prop `locale`, resolved through the\n[`@link-foundation/ui-config`](../ui-config/README.md) layers, so a language\npicker is one user-layer override. Plurals, interpolation, fallbacks and the\ntext direction come from lino-i18n.\n\n```js\nimport { format, parse } from '@link-foundation/ui-core';\nimport { createConfig } from '@link-foundation/ui-config';\nimport {\n  createLocalizer,\n  i18nVocabulary,\n  loadUiCatalogs,\n  message,\n} from '@link-foundation/ui-i18n';\n\nconst document = parse(\n  `(app: document\n  (i18n required)\n  (close: button (label (t ui.dialog.close))))`,\n  { vocabulary: i18nVocabulary() }\n);\nconst config = createConfig({ document });\nconst l = createLocalizer({ config, catalogs: await loadUiCatalogs() });\n\nconfig.set('user', 'app', 'locale', ['ru']); // what a language picker does\nl.text({ type: 'message', key: 'ui.dialog.close' }); // 'Закрыть'\nl.direction(); // 'ltr'\nformat(l.localizeDocument(document));\n// (app: document\n//   (i18n required)\n//   (lang ru)\n//   (dir ltr)\n//   (close: button\n//     (label Закрыть)))\n\nconfig.clear('user'); // back to the platform language, then en\n```\n\nThe complete example, with plurals and a right-to-left locale, is\n`examples/ui-i18n-basics.mjs` in the repository.\n\nRequires Node.js 22.11 or later (the `engines` of lino-i18n 0.5.0), Bun or\nDeno. Everything except `loadCatalogDir` and `loadUiCatalogs` on `file:` URLs\nruns in browsers.\n\nBrowser bundlers select the browser condition of the root entry. You can also\nimport `@link-foundation/ui-i18n/browser` explicitly. Both provide the runtime\nmessage, localizer, vocabulary, lint and catalog parsing helpers, plus\n`loadUiCatalogs()` using `fetch`. The shipped catalog is tracked as an asset\nand works with emitted or inlined Vite assets. Filesystem-only\n`loadCatalogDir` and `UI_LOCALES_URL` stay on the default Node root entry.\n\n## Writing messages: `(t ...)`\n\nA message stands where literal text would:\n\n| Form                                        | Meaning                                           |\n| ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |\n| `(label (t ui.dialog.close))`               | the prop `label` is the message `ui.dialog.close` |\n| `(t greeting (name 'Ada'))`                 | params, interpolated as `{name}` or `{{name}}`    |\n| `(t files (count 3))`                       | `count` picks the CLDR plural form                |\n| `(t greeting (name (t ui.settings.title)))` | a param may be a message too                      |\n| `(greeting: text (t greeting))`             | `t` on an element: its first positional value     |\n\nKeys are dotted paths of the catalog. Number atoms of params are numbers;\nanything else is text. `parseMessage` reads a raw link\n(`{ type: 'message', key, params }`), `message(key, params)` creates one and\n`messageRaw` writes one back; `typeValue` is ui-core `values.typeValue` with\nthe `message` type (a malformed `(t)` is an `invalid-value` error with\n`expected: 'message'`).\n\nui-core reads documents with a fixed vocabulary. With the default one, `(t ...)`\non an element and `(locale ...)`, `(dir ...)` and `(i18n ...)` on the root are\nkept as unknown sublinks (with a warning) and this package still reads them.\nParse with `i18nVocabulary()` to make them props: then there are no warnings and\nui-config sees `(locale ...)` of the document as a `site` value.\n\n| Root prop                   | Meaning                                                      |\n| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |\n| `(locale ru)`               | the locale of the document (a ui-config prop)                |\n| `(i18n required\\|optional)` | `required`: literal text is an error (`check:i18n`)          |\n| `(dir ltr\\|rtl)`            | written by `localizeDocument`; any earlier value is replaced |\n\n## Choosing the locale\n\n`l.locale()` is the first of:\n\n1. the root prop `locale` resolved through the config layers (session, user,\n   site, theme, defaults), on `options.root` (default `config.base`);\n2. `options.locale` or the last `setLocale` (without a config);\n3. `determineLocale(navigator.languages, approved)` (`options.languages`\n   replaces `navigator.languages`; pass `[]` for deterministic tests);\n4. `defaultLocale` (`en`).\n\nThe result is matched to the approved locales (default: the locales of the\ncatalogs), so `ru-RU` becomes `ru`; a locale that is not approved is kept as\nis, and its messages fall back to `defaultLocale`.\n\n`l.setLocale('ru')` writes the user layer (`options.layer` for `session`),\n`l.setLocale(null)` removes the override. `l.subscribe((locale, previous) => …)`\nis called once per change of the locale, whatever changed it.\n\n## Text\n\n`l.text(value, params?)` (and `resolveText(value, l, params?)`):\n\n- strings are returned unchanged;\n- messages and raw `(t ...)` links are looked up in the locale, then in\n  `defaultLocale`;\n- a key missing in every locale returns the key and calls\n  `onMissing(key, locale)`.\n\n`l.localizeDocument(doc)` returns a copy of a parsed document with every\nmessage replaced by its text and the root marked with `(lang …)` and\n`(dir …)`, ready for a renderer. /tmp/gh-issue-solver-1795594347603/docs/case-studies/issue-6/README.md <<'EOF'\n# Issue 6 case study\n\n[Issue 6](https://github.com/link-foundation/universal-translator/issues/6)\nasks for a set of fixes and improvements on top of the issue 1 translator:\nmeta-language views, a forgiving language switch, random examples, language\nversions and variants, semantic primes for every natural language, a UI\nsettings panel backed by [link-foundation/ui](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui),\nconcrete syntax tree (CST) fidelity for whitespace and comments, a separate\ncomment language, a standards editor with recursive word definitions and\nWikidata lookups, and a re-check of every issue 1 requirement.\n\nThe [requirements inventory](requirements.md) lists every requirement with\nits solution and evidence; [requirements.lino](requirements.lino) is the\nmachine-readable copy that `scripts/check-requirements.mjs` checks in CI.\n\n## Evidence collected\n\nThe [data directory](data/) holds Links Notation snapshots (made with\n`experiments/case-study-snapshot.mjs`, round-trip checked against the\nGitHub JSON) of:\n\n- [issue 6](data/issue-6.lino) and its comments (none at the time of writing);\n- [PR 7](data/pr-7.lino), the pull request for this issue;\n- [issue 1](data/issue-1.lino), whose requirements are re-checked here.\n\n## Observations before the change\n\nA JavaScript program with an indented comment, blank lines, a two-line\nblock comment and a trailing comment was translated to Python with the 0.12\nlibrary:\n\n- the leading spaces inside `//   indented comment` were trimmed;\n- the second line of the block comment was emitted without `#`, which is\n  not valid Python;\n- blank lines between statements disappeared;\n- the trailing comment moved to a line of its own.\n\nThe demo app listed 4 fixed samples (Statement, Function, Program,\nSentence), translated the left editor only, failed with an error whenever the\nleft language changed to one that could not read the current text, showed\nevery profile of English as its own language, and had no settings.\n\n## Online research\n\n- **Natural Semantic Metalanguage.** Goddard and Wierzbicka list 65 semantic\n  primes with exponents documented for dozens of languages\n  ([NSM homepage](https://intranet.secure.griffith.edu.au/schools-departments/natural-semantic-metalanguage),\n  [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_semantic_metalanguage)).\n  Primes are a vocabulary *restriction* (a \"dictionary modifier\"), so every\n  natural language gets a `minimal` variant that only allows prime exponents\n  plus a few grammatical words.\n- **Small standard vocabularies.** Sizes of known controlled vocabularies,\n  used to pick the default \"biggest standard that is still small enough\"\n  (≤ 1024 words):\n\n  | Standard | Size |\n  | --- | --- |\n  | NSM semantic primes | 65 |\n  | Toki Pona | about 120–137 |\n  | Basic English (Ogden) | 850 |\n  | ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English | about 900 approved words |\n  | Globish (Nerrière) | 1500 (over the limit) |\n  | VOA Special English | about 1500 (over the limit) |\n  | Longman Defining Vocabulary | about 2000 (over the limit) |\n\n  Basic English (850) is the largest classical standard under 1024 words,\n  so the size cap is 1024 and Basic English is the default \"biggest\n  small standard\" for English. Other languages use their own descriptions,\n  capped at the same size.\n- **Wikidata.** The\n  [`wbsearchentities`](https://www.wikidata.org/w/api.php?action=help&modules=wbsearchentities)\n  and [`wbgetentities`](https://www.wikidata.org/w/api.php?action=help&modules=wbgetentities)\n  APIs return labels and short descriptions per language, with CORS through\n  `origin=*`. A description is a short noun phrase (\"domesticated animal\"),\n  which is exactly what a recursive definer needs. Lexemes\n  (`L` entities) carry senses with glosses for many languages.\n- **Concrete syntax trees.** [LibCST](https://github.com/Instagram/LibCST)\n  (Python) and [tree-sitter](https://tree-sitter.github.io/) keep every token\n  and its trivia (whitespace and comments). Roslyn calls them *leading* and\n  *trailing trivia*. The translator follows the same model: each statement\n  carries the blank lines and comments before it and an optional trailing\n  comment, and comment text is kept byte for byte.\n- **English variants.** Browsers expose the preferred languages through\n  `navigator.languages` (for example `en-GB`); the app maps `en-GB`, `en-AU`,\n  `en-NZ`, `en-IE`, `en-IN` and `en-ZA` to British spelling and every other\n  English locale to American spelling.\n- **Python versions.** Python 2 used the `print` statement\n  (`print \"x\"`) and `/` for integer division of integers; Python 3 uses\n  `print(...)` and `//` ([PEP 3105](https://peps.python.org/pep-3105/),\n  [PEP 238](https://peps.python.org/pep-0238/)).\n\n## Existing components and libraries\n\n| Need | Component | Use |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| UI settings, themes, skins, i18n | [`@link-foundation/ui-settings`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@link-foundation/ui-settings), [`ui-themes`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@link-foundation/ui-themes), [`ui-tokens`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@link-foundation/ui-tokens), [`ui-i18n`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@link-foundation/ui-i18n) | Settings schema, theme/skin CSS, localized UI strings with RTL |\n| CST and trivia | tree-sitter, LibCST, Roslyn trivia | Design reference; the translator's own parser keeps trivia |\n| Semantic primes | NSM tables | `data/natural/semantic-primes.lino` |\n| Vocabulary lookups | Wikidata API | `js/src/natural/wikidata.js` with a cache and a test pre-cache |\n| Data format | [Links Notation](https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation) | All standards and the requirement inventory |\n\n## Solutions\n\nSee [requirements.md](requirements.md) for the per-requirement plan and\nthe evidence that each one is delivered.\nEOF"

One settings schema,\nwritten in Links Notation, gives:\n\n- coercion of every value (clamping, rounding, rejecting unknown options);\n- merging of untrusted values (storage, links, documents) that never throws;\n- diff-only values documents and share links (`#settings=…`);\n- presets and the active preset, randomised looks with locked keys;\n- versioned migrations, readers for the share links Each link is written either\n`(id: kind clauses…)` or `(kind id clauses…)`; a link with an id and no kind\nis a setting.\n\n```\nschema    = (id: schema (version N))\nsection   = (id: section [(label 'Text')] [(description 'Text')])\nsetting   = (key: (type T) (default V…) clause…)\n          | (key: setting (type T) (default V…) clause…)\npreset    = (preset id [(label 'Text')] [(description 'Text')] (set key V…)…)\nmigration = (migration (from N) (to M) (rename old new)… (old-default key V…)…)\n```\n\nClauses of a setting:\n\n| Clause                                  | Meaning                                                                                                                                                |\n| --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |\n| `(type T)`                              | `range`, `number`, `toggle`, `choice`, `color`, `text` or a type added with `defineFieldType`.                                                         |\n| `(default V…)`                          | The default; it must coerce without change (`(default 99)` above `max` is an error).                                                                   |\n| `(min N)` `(max N)` `(step N)`          | Bounds and step of `range` (required: `min`, `max`) and `number`; values are clamped and rounded to the step grid that starts at `min`.                |\n| `(unit U)`                              | Appended to the CSS value (`24px`).                                                                                                                    |\n| `(options a b c)`                       | The options of `choice` (required).                                                                                                                    |\n| `(label 'Text')` `(description 'Text')` | For generated settings panels.                                                                                                                         |\n| `(section id)`                          | The section of the setting (an unknown section is a warning).                                                                                          |\n| `(comfort)`                             | A comfort setting: kept from the viewer when a shared look is opened, never randomised, ignored by `activePreset`. Presets that set one get a warning. |\n| `(apply (css-var --name))`              | Set as a CSS custom property on `<html>`.                                                                                                              |\n| `(apply (data-attr name))`              | Set as the attribute `data-name` on `<html>`.                                                                                                          |\n| anything else                           | Kept in `field.props` for custom types.                                                                                                                |\n\nKeys are names such as `liquid.blur` (letters, digits, `.`, `-`, `_`).\n`readSchema` never throws: problems are diagnostics (`missing-type`,\n`unknown-type`, `missing-default`, `bad-default`, `missing-range`,\n`missing-options`, `duplicate-key`, `bad-key`, `unknown-key`, `bad-value`,\n`bad-migration`, `bad-version`, `unknown-link`, `unknown-section`,\n`preset-sets-comfort`, `missing-schema-version`, syntax errors), and fields\nwith errors are left out of the schema.\n\n### Field types\n\n| Type     | Value                    | Raw values accepted                            | Random             |\n| -------- | ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------- | ------------------ |\n| `range`  | number in `[min, max]`   | numbers and decimal atoms (`'24'`, `'-0.5'`)   | on the step grid   |\n| `number` | number (bounds optional) | same                                           | when bounded       |\n| `toggle` | `true` / `false`         | booleans, `'true'`, `'false'`                  | yes                |\n| `choice` | one of `options`         | option strings (numbers are compared as text)  | one of the options |\n| `color`  | `#rrggbb`                | `#rrggbb` strings (`red`, `#fff` are rejected) | yes                |\n| `text`   | string                   | strings and numbers                            | never              |\n\n```js\nimport { defineFieldType } from '@link-foundation/ui-settings';\n\ndefineFieldType('vector3', {\n  coerce(field, raw) {\n    const parts = (Array.isArray(raw) ? raw : String(raw).split(' ')).map(\n      Number\n    );\n    return parts.length === 3 && parts.every(Number.isFinite)\n      ? { ok: true, value: parts }\n      : { ok: false };\n  },\n  equals: (a, b) => a.every((n, i) => n === b[i]),\n  random: (field, random) => [random(), random(), random()],\n  format: (field, value) => value.map(String), // (light.direction 0 0 1)\n});\n```\n\n`coerce` is required; `equals` defaults to structural equality, `random` to\n\"not randomised\", `format` to the value as atoms and `css` to the formatted\natoms joined with spaces. A `coerce` that throws counts as a rejected value.\n\n## Values\n\nValues are a plain object with a value for every field. Documents and share\nlinks hold only the values that differ from the defaults:\n\n```\n(settings (version 2) (liquid.blur 24))\n```\n\n| Function                                        | Result                                                                                                                       |\n| ----------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| `defaults(schema)`                              | Every default.                                                                                                               |\n| `merge(schema, base, untrusted)`                | `{ values, rejected }`: unknown keys, `__proto__` and values that do not coerce are rejected. Never throws.                  |\n| `diff(schema, values)`                          | Only the changed values, in schema order.                                                                                    |\n| `isDefault(schema, key, value)`                 | Whether the value is the default.                                                                                            |\n| `reset(schema, values, keys?)`                  | Some keys (default: all) back to the default.                                                                                |\n| `countCustomized(schema, values)`               | How many values differ from the defaults.                                                                                    |\n| `equalValues(schema, a, b, { skip })`           | Field-by-field equality; key order does not matter.                                                                          |\n| `applyPreset(schema, values, id)`               | The values with the preset applied (comfort settings keep their values).                                                     |\n| `activePreset(schema, values)`                  | The id of the preset the values match (ignoring comfort settings and key order), or `null`.                                  |\n| `randomize(schema, values, { random, locked })` | A random look; `random` is required, so a seeded generator gives the same look every time; comfort and locked keys are kept. |\n\n## Documents and share links\n\n| Function                                                | Result                                                                                                                |\n| ------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| `toLino(schema, values)`                                | `(settings (version N) (key value…)…)` of the changed values.                                                         |\n| `fromLino(schema, text, { base, look })`                | `{ ok, values, rejected, version, diagnostics }`, migrated to the schema version.                                     |\n| `fromLegacyJson(schema, json, { version, base, look })` | The JSON settings of the earlier sites.                                                                               |\n| `toShareHash(schema, values)`                           | `#settings=<encodeURIComponent(values document)>`.                                                                    |\n| `fromShareHash(schema, hash, viewerValues)`             | Reads `#settings=(settings …)`, `#settings={…}` (konard.github.io) and `#ui={…}` (immortality); `format` tells which. |\n\nShare links carry a shared _look_: when one is opened, every comfort setting\nkeeps the viewer's value. Hashes longer than `MAX_SHARE_HASH` (8 KiB) are\nrejected with the diagnostic `hash-too-large`, and nothing a link holds can\nthrow: bad encodings, bad JSON and unknown keys become diagnostics and\n`rejected` keys.\n\n## Migrations\n\n`(migration (from 1) (to 2) (rename blur liquid.blur) (old-default liquid.blur 12))`\nmoves version 1 values to version 2:\n\n1. keys are renamed (`blur` → `liquid.blur`);\n2. stored values equal to the old default are dropped, so the user gets the\n   new default (`(blur 12)` → `liquid.blur 18`, `(blur 30)` → `liquid.blur 30`);\n3. the result is merged onto the defaults (or `base`).\n\nMigrations chain (1 → 2 → 3). A shared look from an old version (`look: true`,\nused for share links) is different: the sender saw the old defaults, so\nmissing keys take the old defaults. A newer version than the schema is read\nas it is, with the warning `newer-version`.\n\n## Applying values before paint\n\n`applyToRoot(schema, values, root = document.documentElement)` sets the CSS\nvariables and data attributes of every applied setting (invalid values get the\ndefault).\n\nThe first paint must already use the stored values, so the page inlines a\nsmall script at the top of `<head>`:\n\n```js\nimport {\nShell cwd was reset to /tmp/gh-issue-solver-1795594347603",

Write the settings as a schema with `(version 2)`; mark `animations`,\n   `sound` and `volume` as `(comfort)`.\n2. Write the defaults of the unversioned links as\n   `(migration (from 1) (to 2) (old-default palette mission) …)` (the\n   `LEGACY_V1_BASE` object of the site).\n3. Read stored JSON with `fromLegacyJson(schema, json)` (`v` is the version,\n   an object without `v` is version 1) and store `toLino(schema, values)`.\n4. Read links with `fromShareHash(schema, location.hash, viewerValues)`:\n   `#ui=` links open as before, the viewer's comfort settings win.\n5. Write links with `toShareHash`.\n\n### From konard.github.io (`#settings=` JSON)\n\nThe site keeps flat dotted keys (`{ \"liquid.blur\": 24 }`) in storage and in\n`#settings=<encodeURIComponent(JSON)>` links, without a version.\n\n1. Use the dotted keys as setting keys; the JSON has the schema's version.\n2. Read stored JSON with\n   `fromLegacyJson(schema, json, { version: schema.version })`.\n3. `fromShareHash` tells the old links (`format: 'konard-json'`) from the new\n   ones (`format: 'lino'`) by their first character, so both keep working\n   under the same `#settings=` parameter.\n4. Replace the inline theme script with `beforePaintScript(schema)` and its\n   CSP hash.\n\n## License\n\n[Unlicense](LICENSE)\n\nSee [control and settings integration contracts](../../docs/case-studies/issue-210/contracts.md)\nfor external labels, popup sizing, live editors, rich panel extensions, normalization\nand compatibility codec hooks. The [rich panel example](../ui-components/examples/rich-settings.html)\ndemonstrates conditional fields, section tabs, previews and whole-section columns.\n\nSee the [settings gallery guide](../../docs/case-studies/issue-231/README.md)\nfor balanced columns, preset cards, saved looks, colour popovers and cross-tab sync.\n======\n# @link-foundation/ui-i18n\n\nLocalisation of [`@link-foundation/ui-core`](../ui-core/README.md) documents\nwith [lino-i18n](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-i18n) (pinned to\n0.5.0). Documents refer to catalog messages with `(t KEY)`; the locale is the\nroot prop `locale`, resolved through the\n[`@link-foundation/ui-config`](../ui-config/README.md) layers, so a language\npicker is one user-layer override. Plurals, interpolation, fallbacks and the\ntext direction come from lino-i18n.\n\n```js\nimport { format, parse } from '@link-foundation/ui-core';\nimport { createConfig } from '@link-foundation/ui-config';\nimport {\n  createLocalizer,\n  i18nVocabulary,\n  loadUiCatalogs,\n  message,\n} from '@link-foundation/ui-i18n';\n\nconst document = parse(\n  `(app: document\n  (i18n required)\n  (close: button (label (t ui.dialog.close))))`,\n  { vocabulary: i18nVocabulary() }\n);\nconst config = createConfig({ document });\nconst l = createLocalizer({ config, catalogs: await loadUiCatalogs() });\n\nconfig.set('user', 'app', 'locale', ['ru']); // what a language picker does\nl.text({ type: 'message', key: 'ui.dialog.close' }); // 'Закрыть'\nl.direction(); // 'ltr'\nformat(l.localizeDocument(document));\n// (app: document\n//   (i18n required)\n//   (lang ru)\n//   (dir ltr)\n//   (close: button\n//     (label Закрыть)))\n\nconfig.clear('user'); // back to the platform language, then en\n```\n\nThe complete example, with plurals and a right-to-left locale, is\n`examples/ui-i18n-basics.mjs` in the repository.\n\nRequires Node.js 22.11 or later (the `engines` of lino-i18n 0.5.0), Bun or\nDeno. Everything except `loadCatalogDir` and `loadUiCatalogs` on `file:` URLs\nruns in browsers.\n\nBrowser bundlers select the browser condition of the root entry. You can also\nimport `@link-foundation/ui-i18n/browser` explicitly. Both provide the runtime\nmessage, localizer, vocabulary, lint and catalog parsing helpers, plus\n`loadUiCatalogs()` using `fetch`. The shipped catalog is tracked as an asset\nand works with emitted or inlined Vite assets. Filesystem-only\n`loadCatalogDir` and `UI_LOCALES_URL` stay on the default Node root entry.\n\n## Writing messages: `(t ...)`\n\nA message stands where literal text would:\n\n| Form                                        | Meaning                                           |\n| ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |\n| `(label (t ui.dialog.close))`               | the prop `label` is the message `ui.dialog.close` |\n| `(t greeting (name 'Ada'))`                 | params, interpolated as `{name}` or `{{name}}`    |\n| `(t files (count 3))`                       | `count` picks the CLDR plural form                |\n| `(t greeting (name (t ui.settings.title)))` | a param may be a message too                      |\n| `(greeting: text (t greeting))`             | `t` on an element: its first positional value     |\n\nKeys are dotted paths of the catalog. Number atoms of params are numbers;\nanything else is text. `parseMessage` reads a raw link\n(`{ type: 'message', key, params }`), `message(key, params)` creates one and\n`messageRaw` writes one back; `typeValue` is ui-core `values.typeValue` with\nthe `message` type (a malformed `(t)` is an `invalid-value` error with\n`expected: 'message'`).\n\nui-core reads documents with a fixed vocabulary. With the default one, `(t ...)`\non an element and `(locale ...)`, `(dir ...)` and `(i18n ...)` on the root are\nkept as unknown sublinks (with a warning) and this package still reads them.\nParse with `i18nVocabulary()` to make them props: then there are no warnings and\nui-config sees `(locale ...)` of the document as a `site` value.\n\n| Root prop                   | Meaning                                                      |\n| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |\n| `(locale ru)`               | the locale of the document (a ui-config prop)                |\n| `(i18n required\\|optional)` | `required`: literal text is an error (`check:i18n`)          |\n| `(dir ltr\\|rtl)`            | written by `localizeDocument`; any earlier value is replaced |\n\n## Choosing the locale\n\n`l.locale()` is the first of:\n\n1. the root prop `locale` resolved through the config layers (session, user,\n   site, theme, defaults), on `options.root` (default `config.base`);\n2. `options.locale` or the last `setLocale` (without a config);\n3. `determineLocale(navigator.languages, approved)` (`options.languages`\n   replaces `navigator.languages`; pass `[]` for deterministic tests);\n4. `defaultLocale` (`en`).\n\nThe result is matched to the approved locales (default: the locales of the\ncatalogs), so `ru-RU` becomes `ru`; a locale that is not approved is kept as\nis, and its messages fall back to `defaultLocale`.\n\n`l.setLocale('ru')` writes the user layer (`options.layer` for `session`),\n`l.setLocale(null)` removes the override. `l.subscribe((locale, previous) => …)`\nis called once per change of the locale, whatever changed it.\n\n## Text\n\n`l.text(value, params?)` (and `resolveText(value, l, params?)`):\n\n- strings are returned unchanged;\n- messages and raw `(t ...)` links are looked up in the locale, then in\n  `defaultLocale`;\n- a key missing in every locale returns the key and calls\n  `onMissing(key, locale)`.\n\n`l.localizeDocument(doc)` returns a copy of a parsed document with every\nmessage replaced by its text and the root marked with `(lang …)` and\n`(dir …)`, ready for a renderer. The source document is not changed.\n\n## Right-to-left locales\n\n`l.direction()` and `localeDirection(locale)` are lino-i18n\n`getLocaleDirection`: `rtl` for Arabic, Hebrew, Persian, Urdu and other\nright-to-left scripts, `ltr` otherwise (and for an invalid tag).\n`localizeDocument` writes it as `(dir rtl)` on the root; renderers map it to\n`dir=\"rtl\"` and should use logical CSS properties (`margin-inline-start`, not\n`margin-left`) so that layouts mirror.\n\n## Catalogs\n\n`locales/ui.lino` holds the messages of the framework itself (`ui.dialog.close`,\n`ui.dialog.ok`, `ui.dialog.cancel`, `ui.settings.title`, `ui.settings.reset`,\n`ui.locale.label`) in en, ru, zh and hi, in the lino-i18n format:\n\n```\nen\n  ui\n    dialog\n      close \"Close\"\nru\n  ui\n    dialog\n      close \"Закрыть\"\n```\n\nPlural keys list their CLDR forms (`one`, `few`, `many`, `other`, …):\n\n```\nShell cwd was reset to /tmp/gh-issue-solver-1795594347603",

The [rich panel example](../ui-components/examples/rich-settings.html)\ndemonstrates conditional fields, section tabs, previews and whole-section columns.\n\nSee the [settings gallery guide](../../docs/case-studies/issue-231/README.md)\nfor balanced columns, preset cards, saved looks, colour popovers and cross-tab sync.\n======\n# @link-foundation/ui-i18n\n\nLocalisation of [`@link-foundation/ui-core`](../ui-core/README.md) documents\nwith [lino-i18n](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-i18n) (pinned to\n0.5.0). Documents refer to catalog messages with `(t KEY)`; the locale is the\nroot prop `locale`, resolved through the\n[`@link-foundation/ui-config`](../ui-config/README.md) layers, so a language\npicker is one user-layer override. Plurals, interpolation, fallbacks and the\ntext direction come from lino-i18n.\n\n```js\nimport { format, parse } from '@link-foundation/ui-core';\nimport { createConfig } from '@link-foundation/ui-config';\nimport {\n  createLocalizer,\n  i18nVocabulary,\n  loadUiCatalogs,\n  message,\n} from '@link-foundation/ui-i18n';\n\nconst document = parse(\n  `(app: document\n  (i18n required)\n  (close: button (label (t ui.dialog.close))))`,\n  { vocabulary: i18nVocabulary() }\n);\nconst config = createConfig({ document });\nconst l = createLocalizer({ config, catalogs: await loadUiCatalogs() });\n\nconfig.set('user', 'app', 'locale', ['ru']); // what a language picker does\nl.text({ type: 'message', key: 'ui.dialog.close' }); // 'Закрыть'\nl.direction(); // 'ltr'\nformat(l.localizeDocument(document));\n// (app: document\n//   (i18n required)\n//   (lang ru)\n//   (dir ltr)\n//   (close: button\n//     (label Закрыть)))\n\nconfig.clear('user'); // back to the platform language, then en\n```\n\nThe complete example, with plurals and a right-to-left locale, is\n`examples/ui-i18n-basics.mjs` in the repository.\n\nRequires Node.js 22.11 or later (the `engines` of lino-i18n 0.5.0), Bun or\nDeno. Everything except `loadCatalogDir` and `loadUiCatalogs` on `file:` URLs\nruns in browsers.\n\nBrowser bundlers select the browser condition of the root entry. You can also\nimport `@link-foundation/ui-i18n/browser` explicitly. Both provide the runtime\nmessage, localizer, vocabulary, lint and catalog parsing helpers, plus\n`loadUiCatalogs()` using `fetch`. The shipped catalog is tracked as an asset\nand works with emitted or inlined Vite assets. Filesystem-only\n`loadCatalogDir` and `UI_LOCALES_URL` stay on the default Node root entry.\n\n## Writing messages: `(t ...)`\n\nA message stands where literal text would:\n\n| Form                                        | Meaning                                           |\n| ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |\n| `(label (t ui.dialog.close))`               | the prop `label` is the message `ui.dialog.close` |\n| `(t greeting (name 'Ada'))`                 | params, interpolated as `{name}` or `{{name}}`    |\n| `(t files (count 3))`                       | `count` picks the CLDR plural form                |\n| `(t greeting (name (t ui.settings.title)))` | a param may be a message too                      |\n| `(greeting: text (t greeting))`             | `t` on an element: its first positional value     |\n\nKeys are dotted paths of the catalog. Number atoms of params are numbers;\nanything else is text. `parseMessage` reads a raw link\n(`{ type: 'message', key, params }`), `message(key, params)` creates one and\n`messageRaw` writes one back; `typeValue` is ui-core `values.typeValue` with\nthe `message` type (a malformed `(t)` is an `invalid-value` error with\n`expected: 'message'`).\n\nui-core reads documents with a fixed vocabulary. With the default one, `(t ...)`\non an element and `(locale ...)`, `(dir ...)` and `(i18n ...)` on the root are\nkept as unknown sublinks (with a warning) and this package still reads them.\nParse with `i18nVocabulary()` to make them props: then there are no warnings and\nui-config sees `(locale ...)` of the document as a `site` value.\n\n| Root prop                   | Meaning                                                      |\n| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |\n| `(locale ru)`               | the locale of the document (a ui-config prop)                |\n| `(i18n required\\|optional)` | `required`: literal text is an error (`check:i18n`)          |\n| `(dir ltr\\|rtl)`            | written by `localizeDocument`; any earlier value is replaced |\n\n## Choosing the locale\n\n`l.locale()` is the first of:\n\n1. the root prop `locale` resolved through the config layers (session, user,\n   site, theme, defaults), on `options.root` (default `config.base`);\n2. `options.locale` or the last `setLocale` (without a config);\n3. `determineLocale(navigator.languages, approved)` (`options.languages`\n   replaces `navigator.languages`; pass `[]` for deterministic tests);\n4. `defaultLocale` (`en`).\n\nThe result is matched to the approved locales (default: the locales of the\ncatalogs), so `ru-RU` becomes `ru`; a locale that is not approved is kept as\nis, and its messages fall back to `defaultLocale`.\n\n`l.setLocale('ru')` writes the user layer (`options.layer` for `session`),\n`l.setLocale(null)` removes the override. `l.subscribe((locale, previous) => …)`\nis called once per change of the locale, whatever changed it.\n\n## Text\n\n`l.text(value, params?)` (and `resolveText(value, l, params?)`):\n\n- strings are returned unchanged;\n- messages and raw `(t ...)` links are looked up in the locale, then in\n  `defaultLocale`;\n- a key missing in every locale returns the key and calls\n  `onMissing(key, locale)`.\n\n`l.localizeDocument(doc)` returns a copy of a parsed document with every\nmessage replaced by its text and the root marked with `(lang …)` and\n`(dir …)`, ready for a renderer. The source document is not changed.\n\n## Right-to-left locales\n\n`l.direction()` and `localeDirection(locale)` are lino-i18n\n`getLocaleDirection`: `rtl` for Arabic, Hebrew, Persian, Urdu and other\nright-to-left scripts, `ltr` otherwise (and for an invalid tag).\n`localizeDocument` writes it as `(dir rtl)` on the root; renderers map it to\n`dir=\"rtl\"` and should use logical CSS properties (`margin-inline-start`, not\n`margin-left`) so that layouts mirror.\n\n## Catalogs\n\n`locales/ui.lino` holds the messages of the framework itself (`ui.dialog.close`,\n`ui.dialog.ok`, `ui.dialog.cancel`, `ui.settings.title`, `ui.settings.reset`,\n`ui.locale.label`) in en, ru, zh and hi, in the lino-i18n format:\n\n```\nen\n  ui\n    dialog\n      close \"Close\"\nru\n  ui\n    dialog\n      close \"Закрыть\"\n```\n\nPlural keys list their CLDR forms (`one`, `few`, `many`, `other`, …):\n\n```",
